verses.text: Remember your Creator while you are young, before the days of trouble come, and the years come near when you will say, "I find no pleasure in them."
Remember him before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars grow dark, and the clouds come back after the rain;
in the day when the guards of the house tremble, and the strong men bend over, and the grinders stop because they are few, and those who look through the windows see only darkness;
when the doors to the street are shut, and the sound of grinding fades; when people rise up at the sound of a bird, but all their songs grow faint;

when people are afraid of heights and of dangers on the road; when the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, and desire is gone. For people go to their everlasting home, and the mourners walk around in the streets.
Remember him before the silver cord is cut, or the golden bowl is broken, or the jar is smashed at the spring, or the wheel is broken at the well,
and the dust goes back to the earth as it was, and the spirit goes back to God who gave it.
"Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless!"
Besides being wise, the Teacher also taught the people knowledge. Yes, he thought carefully, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
The Teacher searched to find pleasing words, and he wrote what was upright and true.
The words of the wise are like sharp sticks used to drive cattle, and their collected sayings are like nails driven in firmly. They are given by one Shepherd.
Beyond these, my son, be warned: there is no end to making many books, and much study makes the body tired.
This is the end of the matter. Everything has been heard. Have deep respect for God and keep his commands, for this is the whole duty of every person.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether it is good or evil.
